item.title: Xcode Instruments guide, updated for Xcode 27
item.description:
SwiftLee's Antoine van der Lee has updated his long-running Xcode Instruments guide for Xcode 27, walking through the full profile-fix-verify cycle for tracking down slow code, memory problems, and UI hangs with measured evidence instead of guesses. Instruments is free with Xcode and opens via Product → Profile, which builds with the Release configuration so the numbers are realistic — and he recommends profiling on a physical device rather than the Simulator.

The guide centers on Time Profiler: record a flow, check the main thread, then use Hide System Libraries and Invert Call Tree to surface the methods actually doing the work, sorted by weight. New in Xcode 27 are a flame-graph view, a Top Functions view that merges repeated calls into one entry, signpost filtering to isolate a single flow, and Run Comparisons, which diffs a baseline recording against a new one with improvements in green and regressions in red. There's also a section on RocketTrace, a Mac app that ranks trace findings by measured impact and packages them for coding agents.

Sources

  • SwiftLee: Xcode Instruments: Profile, Fix, and Verify Performance
